problem: Wayfinding instruction datasets (R2R, REVERIE, etc.) are human-annotated and tied to a single simulator, mostly Matterport3D. This blocks cross-platform generalization tests, and prior instruction synthesizers (Speaker-style models) must be trained per dataset and only work on Matterport3D.
motivation: A generalist navigation agent should be evaluated across simulators, but instruction-path data exist for only one or two platforms. Off-the-shelf LLMs with in-context learning could produce human-like instructions on any simulator from a few reference examples, with no training.
key_idea: Caption egocentric images along a simulator path using an LLM-BLIP question-answering dialogue, then prompt GPT-3.5-turbo-instruct with a few reference instructions (R2R or REVERIE style) to write a wayfinding instruction, with no training and on any simulator.
insight: Replacing human REVERIE instructions with generated ones changes zero-shot VLN SR by under 1 point for central captions (e.g. GLIP-Nav 16.87 vs 16.32), so generated instructions can stand in for human ones for evaluation. Central-frame captions beat panoramic ones, since summarizing 4 views into one sentence loses information. The appendix qualitative comparison shows that LLM+BLIP dialogue removes ghost objects (stairs, treadmill) that BLIP-only captions produce and that ruin R2R-style instructions.
method: Path and image sampling: generate random paths in a simulator (node paths in Matterport3D, uniform-interval sampling along shortest paths in Habitat and TDW) and collect egocentric images.
LLM+BLIP spatial knowledge: ChatCaptioner-style chain-of-thought conversation in which GPT-3.5 asks BLIP-2 questions about each image, giving detailed captions with fewer hallucinated objects.
In-context instruction synthesis: the prompt lists per-frame captions plus reference texts and asks GPT-3.5-turbo-instruct for a concise instruction in that style, from frame 0 to frame n.

Style constraints: R2R prompt adds the annotator guideline text (multi-sentence directions a smart robot can follow); REVERIE prompt requires one sentence under 20 words ending in a task with an object in the final frame.
Matterport3D frame selection: Central Caption (only the heading-direction image per node) or Panoramic Caption (caption all 4 views, then summarize into under 20 words with the LLM).
Evaluation: user study (30 participants, 3 simulators) and zero-shot VLN on REVERIE (CLIP-Nav, Seq-CLIP-Nav, GLIP-Nav) with human instructions swapped for generated ones.

setting.backbone: GPT-3.5-turbo / GPT-3.5-turbo-instruct (frozen) + BLIP-2 (frozen) for instruction generation; CLIP / GLIP with GPT-3.5 for downstream zero-shot VLN
setting.training_data: none (training-free; few reference instructions from R2R/REVERIE used in the prompt)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB image sequences along paths (Matterport3D panoramas of 4 views, or Habitat/TDW frames)
setting.action_space: not applicable for generation; downstream VLN uses discrete Matterport3D nav-graph hops
setting.simulator: Matterport3D, AI Habitat, ThreeDWorld (REVERIE evaluation on Matterport3D)
setting.privileged: Generation uses the ground-truth path between two nodes/points; downstream VLN uses the standard REVERIE setup

numbers_note: The table prints SPL as 0.05-0.18 (likely a 0-1 fraction, though SR is in percent), so values are copied as printed. Original-instruction baselines are in extra fields. Seq-CLIPNav and CLIP-Nav panoramic rows are omitted.
results: Generated central-caption instructions give zero-shot REVERIE SR within about 1 point of human instructions (CLIP-Nav 5.98 vs 6.57, Seq-CLIPNav 13.94 vs 14.92, GLIP-Nav 16.32 vs 16.87); panoramic captions drop slightly further. In the user study, 83.3% of 30 users found the instructions captured environment details and 73.3% believed an agent could reach the target.
limitations: Quality depends on the VQA/captioning module: ghost objects appear, and LLaVA performs poorly on non-photorealistic VirtualHome images.
The LLM sometimes copies wording from the reference examples.

Evaluation is small: a 30-person user study, and quantitative validation only on REVERIE in Matterport3D with weak zero-shot navigators (SR under 17%). The cross-platform generalizability experiments are proposed but not run.
